question: Determine the number of generators of each type (Type 0 and Type 1) to operate, the power output for each generator type, and the number of startups in each of the five consecutive time periods to minimize the total cost of operation. The total cost includes a base cost of 80 units per Type 0 generator and 79 units per Type 1 generator for each period they are active, a power output cost of 3 units per MW for Type 0 generators and 4 units per MW for Type 1 generators, and a startup cost of 352 units for Type 0 generators and 346 units for Type 1 generators. The total power output from all generators must meet or exceed the demand in each period: 217 MW in period 0, 209 MW in period 1, 194 MW in period 2, 182 MW in period 3, and 164 MW in period 4. Each Type 0 generator must produce at least 34 MW and at most 129 MW when active, and each Type 1 generator must produce at least 34 MW and at most 127 MW when active. The combined maximum output of all active generators must meet or exceed specific capacity requirements: 249.55 MW in period 0, 240.35 MW in period 1, 223.1 MW in period 2, 209.3 MW in period 3, and 188.6 MW in period 4. No more than 1 Type 0 generator and 2 Type 1 generators can be active in any period. The number of startups for each generator type is constrained by the number of generators available and the number of generators active in the previous period. The variables representing the number of generators and startups are general integer variables.

import pyomo.environ as pyo

DATA = {
    # Time periods
    "periods": [0, 1, 2, 3, 4],
    # Generator types
    "types": [0, 1],
    # Demand per period (MW)
    "demand": {0: 217, 1: 209, 2: 194, 3: 182, 4: 164},
    # Capacity requirement per period (MW)
    "capacity_req": {0: 249.55, 1: 240.35, 2: 223.1, 3: 209.3, 4: 188.6},
    # Base cost per active generator per period
    "base_cost": {0: 80, 1: 79},
    # Power output cost per MW
    "power_cost": {0: 3, 1: 4},
    # Startup cost
    "startup_cost": {0: 352, 1: 346},
    # Per-generator min/max output (MW)
    "min_gen": {0: 34, 1: 34},
    "max_gen": {0: 129, 1: 127},
    # Max active generators per type per period
    "max_active": {0: 1, 1: 2},
    # Available generators per type (for startup availability cap)
    "available": {0: 1, 1: 2},
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    model.T = pyo.Set(initialize=d["types"])
    model.P = pyo.Set(initialize=d["periods"])

    # Number of active generators of each type in each period
    # "Determine the number of generators of each type (Type 0 and Type 1) to operate"
    # assumption: bounded by max_active[t] only (active_generator_count_bounds)
    model.n = pyo.Var(
        model.T, model.P,
        within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers,
        bounds=lambda m, t, p: (0, d["max_active"][t]),
    )

    # Power output of each generator type in each period (MW)
    # "the power output for each generator type"
    # assumption: power_output_variable_domain = NonNegativeReals
    model.power = pyo.Var(
        model.T, model.P,
        within=pyo.NonNegativeReals,
    )

    # Number of startups of each type in each period
    # "the number of startups in each of the five consecutive time periods"
    # assumption: general integer, bounded by available[t] (startup_availability_limit)
    model.s = pyo.Var(
        model.T, model.P,
        within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers,
        bounds=lambda m, t, p: (0, d["available"][t]),
    )

    # Objective: minimize total cost
    # "minimize the total cost of operation"
    def obj_rule(m):
        base = sum(d["base_cost"][t] * m.n[t, p] for t in m.T for p in m.P)
        power = sum(d["power_cost"][t] * m.power[t, p] for t in m.T for p in m.P)
        startup = sum(d["startup_cost"][t] * m.s[t, p] for t in m.T for p in m.P)
        return base + power + startup

    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # Demand constraint: total power output must meet or exceed demand
    # "The total power output from all generators must meet or exceed the demand in each period"
    def demand_rule(m, p):
        return sum(m.power[t, p] for t in m.T) >= d["demand"][p]

    model.demand_con = pyo.Constraint(model.P, rule=demand_rule)

    # Capacity requirement: combined max output of active generators >= capacity req
    # "The combined maximum output of all active generators must meet or exceed specific capacity requirements"
    # assumption: capacity_requirement_form = sum_t max_gen[t]*n[t,p] >= capacity_req[p]
    def cap_rule(m, p):
        return sum(d["max_gen"][t] * m.n[t, p] for t in m.T) >= d["capacity_req"][p]

    model.cap_con = pyo.Constraint(model.P, rule=cap_rule)

    # Per-generator min/max output linkage
    # "Each Type 0 generator must produce at least 34 MW and at most 129 MW when active"
    # assumption: per_generator_min_max_output_linkage
    def min_out_rule(m, t, p):
        return m.power[t, p] >= d["min_gen"][t] * m.n[t, p]

    model.min_out_con = pyo.Constraint(model.T, model.P, rule=min_out_rule)

    def max_out_rule(m, t, p):
        return m.power[t, p] <= d["max_gen"][t] * m.n[t, p]

    model.max_out_con = pyo.Constraint(model.T, model.P, rule=max_out_rule)

    # Startup linkage for period 0
    # "The number of startups for each generator type is constrained by the number of generators available and the number of generators active in the previous period."
    # assumption: startup_linkage_constraint s[t,0] >= n[t,0]
    def startup_first_rule(m, t):
        return m.s[t, 0] >= m.n[t, 0]

    model.startup_first_con = pyo.Constraint(model.T, rule=startup_first_rule)

    # Startup linkage for periods p >= 1
    # assumption: startup_linkage_constraint s[t,p] >= n[t,p] - n[t,p-1]
    def startup_link_rule(m, t, p):
        if p == 0:

        return m.s[t, p] >= m.n[t, p] - m.n[t, p - 1]

    model.startup_link_con = pyo.Constraint(model.T, model.P, rule=startup_link_rule)

    return model

            return m.s[t, p] <= d["available"][t]
        return m.s[t, p] <= d["available"][t] - m.n[t, p - 1]

    model.startup_avail_con = pyo.Constraint(model.T, model.P, rule=startup_avail_rule)

    return model
